title: Singlet sector of the vector model with angular potential
abstract: We study the singlet sector of large-$N$, $O(N)$ vector model on $S^1_β\times S^2_r$ in presence of an angular potential $Ω$. We compute the free energy of the model both at the free fixed point as well as the non-trivial fixed point. The model undergoes a phase transition when the temperature $T$ and angular potential attain the relation $T^2r^2\sim N (1-ω^2)$, where $ω=rΩ$ and $r$ is the radius of $S^2$, with $Tr\gg1$, at both the fixed points, with different numerical coefficients. The transition was studied earlier at zero angular potential at $Tr\sim \sqrt{N}$. The holonomy eigenvalue distribution, having support on the full circle below the transition, develops a gap above it, called the Gross-Witten-Wadia transition. The angular potential introduces an additional parameter to such a transition, tuning it, the transition can occur even at a fixed temperature. We show that for the free model transition can occur as $1-ω^2\sim 1/N$ while $Tr\sim O(1)$. For the interacting model the computation is performed at a limit $Tr\gg1$, thus we show the same at a large but fixed temperature which does not scale as $\sqrt{N}$. In the ungapped phase, the free energy exhibits a double pole near $ω^2=1$ for both the fixed points. This is possibly due to the fact that the theory projected onto the singlets is non-local and therefore need not obey the leading simple pole scaling of a local thermal effective action.
summary: This paper analyzes the phase transitions of a large-N O(N) vector model on a sphere with an added angular potential. Using advanced techniques like the large-N limit and saddle-point approximation, the authors determine the critical conditions for the Gross-Witten-Wadia transition. The work shows how the potential tunes this transition and reveals non-trivial features in the free energy near the critical points.
main_problem: The study investigates the singlet sector of the large-N, O(N) vector model subjected to an angular potential $\Omega$. The core goal is to analyze the phase transitions occurring in this system.
main_result: The angular potential modifies the Gross-Witten-Wadia transition, allowing it to occur even at fixed temperature. The free energy exhibits a double pole in the ungapped phase, suggesting non-local physics.
method: The analysis employs the large-N limit, utilizing Hubbard-Stratonovich transformations and saddle-point approximations to evaluate the free energy and determine critical lines.
model_or_system: The model is the O(N) vector model defined on $S^1 	imes S^2_r$, restricted to its singlet sector by averaging over the O(N) holonomy. The Hamiltonian includes a term proportional to the angular potential $\Omega$.
key_observables: Free energy ($\log Z_{	ext{sing}}$), critical temperature ($T_{	ext{cr}}$), and the holonomy eigenvalue distribution.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), angular potential ($\Omega$), radius of $S^2$ ($r$), and the large-N limit ($N$).
main_assumptions: The calculations rely on the large-N limit and the saddle-point approximation for evaluating the partition function integral.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the large-N free-theory GW-W phase boundary in the $T_r - N(\dots)$ plane.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the system and implementing the singlet projection. It then calculates the free energy at both fixed points, derives the critical transition condition, and analyzes the effect of the angular potential and subleading corrections.
why_interesting: The study of phase transitions in complex field theories, especially those involving geometric constraints (like the singlet sector) and external potentials, provides deep insights into critical phenomena relevant to condensed matter systems.
